newsitem.title: POLAND: President aide Belka made Polish finance minister.
newsitem.headline: President aide Belka made Polish finance minister.

text.p: President Aleksander Kwasniewski on Tuesday appointed his economic adviser Marek Belka as Poland's new finance minister after accepting the resignation of Grzegorz Kolodko.
Kwasniewski, at a ceremony in his palace, said the choice of Belka, 45, would guarantee Poland stayed on the right economic track.

"I am happy that Professor Belka is appointed to the new post because he is an outstanding personality and his economic views guarantee that the policy of economic growth, the fight against inflation and privatisation is continued," he said.
Kwasniewski praised Kolodko for his three years in office.
"I want to thank Mr Grzegorz Kolodko, who...has filled the most difficult post in the government and his 1112 days in office was our joint success," Kwasniewski said.

Belka, an independent economist who has been advising Kwasniewski on economic policy since his inauguration in late 1995, told Reuters earlier on Tuesday he wanted to continue the government's policy of macroeconomic consolidation, fiscal restraint and fighting inflation.
He said he also wanted to play a more active role in pushing through key structural reforms such as the overhaul of the country's inefficient social security system.

Kolodko, a non-party economist who was finance minister since 1994 in successive governments of the ruling two-party coalition, is credited with maintaining fiscal discipline and continuing some of the market reforms begun by Solidarity-led governments after the 1989 fall of communism.

Kolodko said after the ceremony that he was stepping down at a time when several key economic targets have been achieved including Poland's membership of the OECD and the country was beginning the campaign for parliamentary elections late this year.
"We have managed to bring Poland onto a sustainable growth path, we have a market economy, we are in the OECD and after three years my mission is coming to an end," Kolodko said.
"Now we are entering an election campaign in which I do not want and will not take part," he added.
